rashi.eng: *For Solomon had made.* This refers back to “opposite all the congregation of Israel,” i.e., how was he higher than all of them to make his words heard?

rashi.heb:
*ויעמוד עליו.* 
ועתה יכולין לראותו כל ישראל ומשום שמפסיק הענין צריך לומר כבראשונה נגד כל קהל ישראל וכן ויפרוש כפיו השמימה:
rashi.eng: *and he stood on it.* And now, all Israel could see him, and since he interrupted the topic, he had to repeat, “opposite all the congregation of Israel,” and so, “and he spread forth his hands toward heaven.”

notes.147: (tn, Heb): “one who keeps the covenant and the loyal love.”
notes.148: (tn, Heb): “who walk before you with all their heart.”

rashi.heb:
*אין כמוך אלהים.* 
ממה שאתה שומר הברית והחסד שאתה גוזר מן השמים לתת לאוהביך אתה מצניעו וגונז הברית והחסד לקיים הבטחתך בארץ:
rashi.eng: *there is no God like You.* insofar as You keep the covenant and the kindness that You decree from heaven to give to those who love You. You hide and conceal the covenant and the kindness to fulfill Your promise on Earth.

rashi.heb:
*ההולכים לפניך.* 
כמו שהלך דוד אבי וזה:
rashi.eng: *who walk before You.* as my father David walked, and this is [the meaning of]

notes.149: (tn, Heb): “[you] who kept to your servant David my father that which you spoke to him.”
notes.150: (tn, Heb): “you spoke by your mouth and by your hand you fulfilled, as this day.”

rashi.heb:
*אשר שמרת לעבדך דוד.* 
בל' אמנת הבטחה:
rashi.eng: *For You have kept for Your servant David.* with an expression referring to the realization of a promise.

notes.151: (tn, Heb): “there will not be cut off from you a man from before me sitting on the throne of Israel.”
notes.152: (tn, Heb): “guard their way by walking in my law as you have walked before me.”

notes.154: (tn, Heb): “Indeed, can God really live with mankind on the earth?” The rhetorical question expects the answer, “Of course not,” the force of which is reflected in the translation “God does not really live with mankind on the earth.”

rashi.heb:
*כי האמנם ישב אלהים את האדם על הארץ.* 
ל' תמיה וכי אפשר שיאמין אדם שישב אלהים על הארץ כי שמים ושמי השמים וגומר אלא מחמת חסד שגמלת לדוד אבי צמצמת שכינתך:
rashi.eng: *But will God indeed dwell with man on the Earth?.* This is an expression of wonder. Is it possible for man to believe that God will dwell on the Earth? For the heaven and the heaven of the heaven, etc. However, because of the kindness that You bestowed upon my father, David, You contracted Your Shechinah.

rashi.heb:
*אף כי הבית הזה אשר בניתי.* 
ולמה בניתיו להתפלל לפני האלהים ולפנות הוא אל תפלתינו:
rashi.eng: *much less this House that I have built.* So why did I build it? To pray before God and so that He should turn to our prayers.

notes.157: (tn, Heb): “the loud cry and the prayer.”

rashi.heb:
*לשמוע אל הרנה.* 
זו צעקה כמו (מלכים א' כ"ב) ותעבר הרנה במחנה ועל כרחך על צעקתם של כל אדם שהוא נס מפני צרתו אל יתפלל אלא בצעקתו בסתר כך חבור המקראות וסוף הענין מוכיח שאמר ואתה תשמע ממקום שבתך למדת שלא בנאו אלא לדעת כן להוריד בו שכינה כדי שישב על הארץ לשמוע ממכון שבתך אל התפלות שיתפללו בו:
rashi.eng: *to the cry.* Heb. הָרִנָּה. This is a cry, like (I Kings 22:36): “A cry (הָרִנָּה) passed through the camp.” Perforce, concerning the cry of any man who flees in distress, he will not pray but express his cry in secret. This is the sequence of the verses, and the conclusion of the topic proves it, for he says, “You shall hear from Your abode.” You have thus learned that he built it only with this intention to bring down the Shechinah therein, in order that He dwell on the Earth, to hear “from Your abode” the prayer that they will pray therein.

notes.159: (tn, Heb): “so your eyes might be open toward this house night and day, toward the place about which you said, ‘My name will be there.’”
notes.160: (tn, Heb): “by listening to the prayer which your servant is praying concerning this place.”

rashi.heb:
*להיות עיניך פתוחות.* 
בכל עת אשר יתפללו אליך:
rashi.eng: *That Your eyes may be open, etc..* whenever they pray to You.

notes.161: (tn, Heb): “listen to the requests of your servant and your people Israel which they are praying concerning this place.”

notes.163: (tn, Heb): “and if the man who sins against his neighbor when one takes up against him a curse to curse him and the curse comes before your altar in this house.”

rashi.heb:
*אם יחטא איש.* 
מקרא זה על כל ישראל המחייב חברו שבועה אם באמת הוא משביעו והנשבע נשבע לשקר אתה תשמע השמים ואם הדין עם הנשבע שבעל הדין מזקיקו על שבועה של חנם אף המשביעו קרוי רשע:
rashi.eng: *If a man sins.* This verse refers to all Israel; whoever exacts an oath from his neighbor - if he is adjuring him legitimately, and the one swearing is swearing falsely, You shall hear from heaven. If, on the other hand, justice is on the side of the one who swears, for the litigant exacts an oath from him for naught, even the one who exacts the oath is called wicked.

notes.164: (tn, Heb): “and you, hear [from] heaven and act and judge your servants by repaying the guilty, to give his way on his head, and to declare the innocent to be innocent, to give to him according to his innocence.”

rashi.heb:
*ולהצדיק צדיק.* 
שלא לענשו על השבועה שהרי באמת הוא נשבע ותוספתא דסוטה מפרש את אשר יחטא, בועל אשת איש, ונשא בו אלה, ויחייב בו אלה כשם שהמים בודקים אותה כך המים בודקין אותו, לפני מזבחך, כדכתיב (במדבר ה׳:י״ח) והעמיד הכהן את האשה:
rashi.eng: *and to justify the righteous.* not to punish him for the oath, for he swore in truth. Tosefta of Sotah (1:3) explains [this verse as referring to the rite of the sotah, the married woman accused of adultery Num. 5:11-30)]: If a man sins by being intimate with a married woman, and an oath be exacted of him and an oath makes him guilty, for just as the water tests her, so does the water test him. before Your altar - as it is written (Num. 5:18): “And the priest shall have the woman stand [before the Lord].”

rashi.heb:
*לתת דרכו בראשו.* 
כדכתיב וצבתה בטנה (שם):
rashi.eng: *to bring his way upon his head.*  as it is written (ibid. verse 27): “her belly will swell and her thigh will fall away.”

rashi.heb:
*ולהצדיק צדיק.* 
דכתיב ונקתה ונזרעה זרע (שם):
rashi.eng: *and to justify the righteous .* (ibid. verse 28): “and she will be blessed with offspring.”

notes.165: (tn): Or “are struck down before an enemy.”
notes.167: (tn, Heb): “and they pray and ask for help.”

rashi.heb:
*ואם ינגף עמך.* 
ולא מפני שידך קצרה מלהושיע אלא דבר זה גורם כי יחטאו לך:
rashi.eng: *And if Your people… is struck down.* not because You have no power, but because they will sin against You.

rashi.heb:
*ושבו והודו את שמך.* 
פתרון והתוודו את עונם והאחרון מוכיח והודו את שמך ומחטאתם ישובון כי תענם:
rashi.eng: *and confess.* Heb. וְהוֹדוּ. The meaning is: and they will confess their iniquity, and the latter verse proves this (verse 26): “and confess to Your name and repent of their sin, so that You may answer them.”

rashi.heb:
*והשיבותם.* 
והשב אותם אל האדמה כי כשנופלים ונגפים לפני אויביהם תופשים מה שיכולים ומביאים אותם בשביה אל ארץ אחרת:
rashi.eng: *and bring them back to the land.* For when they fall and are struck down before their enemies, they [their enemies] will seize what they can and will bring them into captivity to another land.

notes.169: (tn, Heb): “when.” In the Hebrew text vv. 26-27a actually contain one lengthy conditional sentence, which the translation has divided into two sentences for stylistic reasons.
notes.170: (tn): Or “heavens” (also in v. 12). The Hebrew term שָׁמַיִם (shamayim) may be translated “heaven(s)” or “sky” depending on the context.
notes.173: (tn): The Hebrew text reads “because you answer them,” as if the verb is from עָנָה (’anah, “answer”). However, this reference to a divine answer is premature, since the next verse asks for God to intervene in mercy. It is better to revocalize the consonantal text as תְעַנֵּם (t�’annem, “you afflict them”), a Piel verb form from the homonym עָנָה (“afflict”).

rashi.heb:
*בהעצר השמים.* 
כדכתיב ועצר את השמים ולא יהיה מטר (דברים י״א:י״ז):
rashi.eng: *When heaven is shut up.* as it is written (Deut. 11:17): “and He will shut up the heaven, and there will be no rain.”

notes.174: (tn): The present translation understands כִּי (ki) in an emphatic or asseverative sense (“Certainly”). Other translation have “indeed” (NASB), “when” (NRSV), “so” (NEB), or leave the word untranslated (NIV).
notes.175: (tn, Heb): “the good way in which they should walk.”

rashi.heb:
*כי תורם אל הדרך.* 
כמו שעשית כשהיה רעב בימי דוד ג' שנים (שמואל ב כ״א:א׳) והורית ואמרת להם אל שאול ואל בית הדמים כמו כן תורם איזה חטא גורם להם על מה נעצרו השמים:
rashi.eng: *for You will teach them the good way.* as You did when there was a famine in David’s time for three years (II Sam. 21:1), and You taught them and said to them, “(It is) for Saul and (also) for his bloody house.” Likewise, so shall You teach them which sin causes them [their distress], for what reason the heaven was shut up.

notes.177: (tn): Actually two Hebrew words appear here, both of which are usually (but not always) taken as referring to locusts. Perhaps different stages of growth or different varieties are in view, but this is uncertain. NEB has “locusts new-sloughed or fully grown”; NASB has “locust or grasshopper”; NIV has “locusts or grasshoppers”; NRSV has “locust, or caterpillar.”

rashi.heb:
*כל נגע.* 
פתרון הרי זכרתי לך דבר שדפון וירקון נגיפה אף בעצירת גשמים ומה עוד להרבות אלא כל נגע וכל מחלה כי יהיה והתפלל:
rashi.eng: *whatsoever plague, whatsoever sickness (there be).* The meaning is: I have mentioned to You pestilence, blast and mildew, being struck down [in battle], and lack of rainfall, and what else can I include, but whatsoever plague, whatsoever sickness there may be, and he pray and spread forth his hands toward this House, and this is what it says.

notes.179: (tn, Heb): “every prayer, every request for help which will be to all the people, to all your people Israel.”
notes.180: (tn, Heb): “which they know, each his pain and his affliction.”

rashi.heb:
*ופרש כפיו אל הבית הזה.* 
וזה שאמר כל תפלה וכל תחנה שיתפלל ויתחנן על זאת מכל אחד הדברים האלה:
rashi.eng: *Any prayer, any supplication.* that he will pray and supplicate about, concerning any of these matters.

rashi.heb:
*אשר ידעו איש נגעו.* 
כלומר אם יתפלל על נגעו ועל מכאובו להסירו ממנו:
rashi.eng: *every man shall know his plague.* i.e., if he pray about his affliction or about his sickness to remove it from him.

notes.181: (tn): The words “their sin” are not in the Hebrew text, but are supplied for clarification.
notes.182: (tn, Heb): “and act and give to each one according to all his ways because you know his heart.” In the Hebrew text vv. 28-30a actually contain one lengthy conditional sentence, which the translation has divided up for stylistic reasons.
notes.183: (tn, Heb): “Indeed you know, you alone, the heart of all the sons of mankind.”

rashi.heb:
*וסלחת ונתתה לאיש ככל דרכיו וגו'.* 
לרשע כרשעתו ולצדיק כצדקתו שאם לא ישלם לרשע כפי רוע מעלליו יטיח דברים כלפי מעלה ויאמר אין אלהים (אז) יודע לבבו ויהיה חילול השם כמו כן תעשה לצדיק כצדקתו שתעשה לו כשיתפלל לפניך:
rashi.eng: *and forgive and give to each man according to his ways, etc..* to the wicked according to his wickedness and to the righteous according to his righteousness. For if He does not repay the wicked according to his wickedness, he will speak insolently toward Heaven, and he will say, “There is no God.” Then [the thoughts of] his heart will be known, and there will be a profanation of the Name [of God]. Likewise shall You do to the righteous according to his righteousness, which You shall do for him when he prays to You.

rashi.heb:
*למען ייראוך.* 
וישוב הרשע מדרכו ולכך אני מתפלל לתת לו לאיש כדרכיו:
rashi.eng: *That they may fear You.* and the wicked will repent of his way; therefore, I pray to give each man according to his ways.

notes.187: (tn, Heb): “your great name.” The word “name” sometimes refers to one’s reputation or honor (thus the translation here, “your great reputation”).
notes.188: (tn, Heb): “and your strong hand and your outstretched arm.”

notes.189: (tn, Heb): “and do all which the foreigner calls to [i.e., “requests of”] you.”
notes.190: (tn, Heb): “name.” See the note on “reputation” in v. 32.
notes.192: (tn, Heb): “that your name is called over this house which I built.” The Hebrew idiom “call the name over” indicates ownership. See 2 Sam 12:28.

rashi.heb:
*ועשית ככל אשר יקרא אליך הנכרי.* 
בישראל אני מתפלל לתת לו כדרכיו אבל לעו"ג ככל אשר יקרא לך לפי שישראל מכירין בהקב"ה ויודעין שהיכולת בידו לעשות אם אין תפלתו נשמעת תולה בעצמו בחטאיו ומפשפש במעשיו אבל העו"ג קורא תגר ואומר שמעתי שמעו בכל העולם ונתיגעתי בדרכים הרבה עד שבאתי והתפללתי במקום הזה ולא מצאתי בו ממש כשאר אלהות לפיכך ועשית ככל אשר יקרא אליך הנכרי:
rashi.eng: *and You shall do whatever the stranger calls upon You.* Concerning an Israelite, I pray to give him according to his ways, but concerning a heathen, according to all the stranger calls upon You, because Israelites recognize the Holy One, blessed be He, and they know that He has the ability to do, and if his prayer is not heard, he assigns the cause to himself, to his sins, and he searches his deeds, but the heathen will complain of injustice and say, “I heard His fame throughout the world, and I toiled on many roads until I came and prayed in this place, and I did not find reality in Him any more than the other deities.” Therefore, You shall do whatever the stranger calls upon You.

notes.193: (tn, Heb): “When your people go out for battle against their enemies in the way which you send them.”
notes.194: (tn, Heb): “toward this city which you have chosen and the house which I built for your name.”

rashi.heb:
*דרך העיר.* 
פניהם לצד ירושלים:
rashi.eng: *toward the city.* With their faces toward Jerusalem.

notes.195: (tn, Heb): “their prayer and their request for help.”

rashi.heb:
*ועשית משפטם.* 
נקמתם באויביהם ע"א צרכיהם דוגמא לעשות משפט עבדו (מלכים א ח׳:נ״ט):
rashi.eng: *and maintain their cause.* their revenge from their enemies. Another meaning is: their necessities. A similar instance is (I Kings 8:59): “that He sustain the cause of His servant.”

notes.197: (tn, Heb): “they”; the referent (God’s people) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

notes.198: (tn, Heb): “they”; the referent (God’s people) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.199: (tn, Heb): Or “stop and reflect”; “bring back to their heart.”

notes.202: (tn, Heb): “your name.” The word “name” sometimes refers to one’s reputation or honor (thus the translation here, “your honor”).

rashi.heb:
*אשר בניתי לשמך.* 
פתרון הבית הזה אשר בניתי כדי לגדל שמך כי אז כשתקבל תפלתם אז יתפללו לך בבית הזה או בכל מקום שהם ויפנו לביתך זה:
rashi.eng: *that I built for Your name.* The meaning is: this House, which I built in order to aggrandize Your name, for when You accept their prayer, they will pray to You in this House; wherever they are, they will turn to this, Your House.

notes.203: (tn, Heb): “their prayer and their requests for help.”

rashi.heb:
*ושמעת.* 
תפלתם ועל זה יתגדל שמך בעולם:
rashi.eng: *You shall hear, etc..* And through this, Your name will be aggrandized in the world.

notes.205: (tn, Heb): “May your eyes be open and your ears attentive to the prayer of this place.”

notes.207: (tn, Heb): “and may your loyal ones rejoice in good.”

rashi.heb:
*ועתה קומה ה'.* 
שלא להטלטל כאשר עד עתה משילה לנוב ומנוב לגבעון:
rashi.eng: *And now, arise, O Lord.* so as not to have to move as until now, from Shiloh to Nob and from Nob to Gibeon.

rashi.heb:
*אתה וארון עזך.* 
שלא יטלטל עוד מעתה:
rashi.eng: *You and the Ark of Your might.* that it will no longer move from now on.

rashi.heb:
*עזך.* 
על שם כן קרוי עוזך על שעשה נפלאותיו ועזוזות בפלשתים וכן כתיב (לעיל ט"ז) בהודו לה' דרשו ה' ועוזו ועוד אמרו רבותינו במסכת עבודת כוכבים וישרנה הפרות (שמואל א ו׳:י״ב) מה שירה אמרו הושיעה לו ימינו וזרוע קדשו (תהילים צ״ח:א׳):
rashi.eng: *Your might.* Because of the following it is called “Your might:” because it performed wonders and mighty deeds among the Philistines. And so it is written above (I Chron 16: 8-36): “Give thanks to the Lord”, “Search for the Lord and His might.” Our Sages stated further in Tractate Abodah Zarah 24b (I Sam. 6:12): “And the cows sang.” What song did they recite? They said, (Ps. 98:1) “His right hand and His holy arm have gained Him the victory.”

rashi.heb:
*ילבשו תשועה.* 
מחמת שלא יטלטלו ממקום למקום כמו והיה צדק אזור מתניו (ישעיהו י״א:ה׳):
rashi.eng: *shall be attired with salvation.* because they will not wander from place to place, like (Isa. 11:5): “And righteousness shall be the girdle of his loins.”

rashi.heb:
*וחסידיך ישמחו בטוב.* 
ברוב טובות ומעשרות הניתן ללוים בשכר ששומרין את הארון ומשוררים לפניו:
rashi.eng: *and Your pious ones shall rejoice with the goodness.* with the abundance of goodness and tithes that will be given to the Levites as reward for guarding the Ark and singing before it.

notes.208: (tc, Heb): “do not turn away the face of your anointed ones.” Many medieval Hebrew mss, as well as the ancient versions, read the singular, “your anointed,” which would probably refer to Solomon specifically, rather than the people.

rashi.heb:
*אל תשב פני משיחך.* 
מלעשות טובה עמדי ואם לא למעני עשה למענך:
rashi.eng: *do not turn back the face of Your anointed one.* by not treating me with goodness, and if not for my sake, do it for Your sake.

notes.209: (tn): Or “the sky.” The Hebrew term שָׁמַיִם (shamayim) may be translated “heaven(s)” or “sky” depending on the context.

notes.210: (tn): The word “saying” is supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.

notes.211: (tn, Heb): “and the priests were standing at their posts, and the Levites with the instruments of music of the Lord.”
notes.212: (tn, Heb): “which David the king made to give thanks to the Lord, for lasting is his loyal love, when David praised by them.”
notes.213: (tn, Heb): “opposite them”; the referent (the Levites) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*והכהנים על משמרותם.* 
כאשר חלקן דוד לכ"ד משמרות לשרת כל משמרה ומשמרה שבוע שלה והלוים כמו כן על כ"ד משמרות שלהם:
rashi.eng: *And the priests… on their watches.* as David had divided them into twenty-four watches, for each watch to serve its week, and the Levites likewise on their twenty-four watches

rashi.heb:
*להודות.* 
בכלי שיר שהיו אומרים הודו לה' כי טוב כי לעולם חסדו:
rashi.eng: *to give thanks.* with musical instruments, for they recited (Ps. 136): “Give thanks to the Lord for He is good, for His loving kindness is eternal.”

rashi.heb:
*בהלל דויד.* 
הכלי שיר שהיו אומרין בו הלל של דוד וההודיות בידם של לוים:
rashi.eng: *with David’s praise.* The musical instruments with which they recited David’s praise and the thanksgivings were in the Levites’ hands.

rashi.heb:
*והכהנים.* 
מחצרים נגדם שעליהם לשורר בחצוצרות שנאמר ובני אהרן הכהנים יתקעו וגו' (מדבר י'):
rashi.eng: *and the priests were sounding the trumpets opposite them.* For it was incumbent upon them to play music with the trumpets, as it is said (Num. 10:8): “And the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall blow [with the trumpets].”

notes.214: (tc): The Hebrew text omits reference to the grain offerings at this point, but note that they are included both in the list in the second half of the verse (see note on “offerings” at the end of this verse) and in the parallel account in 1 Kgs 8:64. The construction וְאֶת־הַמִּנְחָה (v�’et-hamminkhah; vav [ו] + accusative sign + noun with article; “grain offerings”) was probably omitted accidentally by homoioarcton. Note the וְאֶת (v�’et) that immediately follows.
notes.215: (tn, Heb): “to hold the burnt sacrifices, grain offerings, and the fat of the peace offerings.” Because this is redundant, the translation employs a summary phrase: “all these offerings.”

rashi.heb:
*ויקדש שלמה את תוך החצר.* 
רבותינו חולקין בדבר זה (זבחים נ"ט) רבי יהודה אומר קדש את רצפת העזרה בקדושת מזבח להקטיר על הרצפה כי מזבח הנחשת קטן מהכיל שרבו קרבנות להביא אמר לו רבי יוסי והלא כבר נאמר (לעיל ב' ח') אלף עולות יעלה שלמה על מזבח שעשה משה וכשאתה מגיע לחשבון אמות ומנין עולות תמצא שזה של אבנים גדול משל משה שהמזבח של משה מקום מערכתו אמה על אמה ושל שלמה מקום מערכתו כ"ד על כ"ד הרי של שלמה חמשה מאות ושבעים ושש כשל משה א"כ מה הוא קדש המלך את תוך החצר שקבע בו מזבח של אבנים מחובר ברצפה:
rashi.eng: *And Solomon consecrated the interior of the court.* Our Sages differ in this matter (Zeb. 59): Rabbi Judah says: He consecrated the floor of the forecourt with the sanctity of the altar to burn offerings on the floor, because the copper altar was too small to contain [the offerings], because they brought many sacrifices. Rabbi Jose said to him: Was it not already stated (1:6): “And he offered up on it a thousand burnt offerings” on the altar that Moses had made? When you compute the number of cubits and the number of burnt offerings, you will find that this one of stones was larger than that of Moses, for on Moses’ altar, the place of its pyre was a cubit by a cubit, whereas on Solomon’s, the place of its pyre was twenty-four by twenty-four. The result is that Solomon’s [altar] was 576 times as large as that of Moses. If so, what is the meaning of (I Kings 8:64): “the king consecrated the interior of the court” ? That he set the stone altar into it, fastened to the floor.

rashi.heb:
*לא יכול להכיל.* 
בשל משה הוא אומר כאדם האומר ננס פלוני ופסול לעבודה:
rashi.eng: *could not contain.* He is talking about Moses’ [altar], like a person who says, “So and so is a dwarf and is disqualified from performing the sacrificial service.”

notes.216: (tn, Heb): “Solomon held the festival at that time for seven days, and all Israel was with him, a very great assembly from Lebo Hamath to the wadi of Egypt.”

rashi.heb:
*מלבוא חמת.* 
שהוא בצפון של ארץ ישראל:
rashi.eng: *from the entrance of Hamath.* which is in the north of the land of Israel.

rashi.heb:
*עד נחל מצרים.* 
שהיא כנגדו כמפורש באלה מסעי:
rashi.eng: *to the brook of Egypt.* which is opposite it, as is delineated in אֵלֶּה מַסְעֵי (ibid. verse 5).

notes.217: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Solomon) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.218: (tn): The words “they left” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.

rashi.heb:
*וביום עשרים ושלשה לחדש השביעי שלח את העם.* 
שהוא ט' לחנוכת הבית ובמלכים (א' ח') כתוב וביום השמיני שהוא כ"ב לחדש פתרון ביום ח' נתן להם רשות לילך לאחר החג ולמחר כשיצא החג אז הלכו כולם יחד, ע"א ביום ח' נתן להם רשות ושלח אותם היושבים בתוך תחום שבת וכל מי שירצה ליסע ולילך באותו היום באותו התחום ולמחר שלח כל העם כולו ובב"ר מפרש נטלו רשות ממנו והמתינו עוד שם יום אחד וחזרו ונטלו רשות עוד למחר פעם שניה לכך נאמר ביום כ"ג בחדש:
rashi.eng: *And on the twenty-third day of the seventh month, he dismissed the people.* which was the ninth [day] of the inauguration of the Temple, but in I Kings (8:66) it is written: “On the eighth day,” which was the twenty-second of the month. The meaning is: On the eighth day he gave them permission to leave after the Feast, and on the morrow, when the Feast was over, they all went [home] together. Another meaning: On the eighth day he gave them permission and dismissed those who lived within the Sabbath limits and whoever wished to travel and go on that day in that limit, and on the following day, he dismissed the entire populace. In Genesis Rabbah (35:3) it is explained that they took his leave but waited there one more day and then they repeated [this procedure] and took leave again a second time; therefore it is said: “on the twenty-third day of the month.”

rashi.heb:
*שמחים וטובי לב וגו'.* 
לדויד ולשלמה כי מה שדבר בפיו (לעיל כ"ח) בנך שלמה הוא יבנה בית לשמי מלא בידו שנתן לו בן יושב על כסאו שבנה הבית לשם ה' ובב"ר מפרש א"ר לוי כתיב כי חנוכת וגו' שמחים מוסב על אשר אמר ה' לדוד שקיים מה שנדר לשלמה שבחר בו מכל אחיו כי חכם הוא:
rashi.eng: *rejoicing and delighted of heart, etc. for David, for Solomon.* For that which He spoke with His mouth above (I Chron 28:6): “Your son Solomon - he shall build My House,” He fulfilled with His hand, for He gave him a son sitting on his throne, who built a House in the name of the Lord. And in Genesis Rabbah it is explained: Said Rabbi Levi: It is written: “for the inauguration of, etc.” “Rejoicing” refers to “that the Lord had wrought for David,” viz. that He fulfilled that which He had vowed to Solomon, that He chose him from all his brothers because he was wise.

rashi.heb:
*ולישראל עמו.* 
כדכתיב במלכים (א' ח') לא נפל דבר אחד וגו', ע"א ולישראל עמו שהיה להם מושל שהיו יושבין בבטחון ובהשקט כדכתיב וישב יהודה וישראל וגו' (שם ה'):
rashi.eng: *and for Israel His people.* it is written in I Kings (8:56): “there has not failed one word, etc.” Another explanation: “and for Israel His people” - they had a ruler, so that they dwelt safely and tranquilly, as it is written (ibid. 5:5): “And Judah and Israel dwelt, etc.”

notes.220: (tn, Heb): “and all that entered the heart of Solomon to do in the house of the Lord and in his house he successfully accomplished.”

notes.222: (tn, Heb): “temple of sacrifice.” This means the Lord designated the temple as the place for making sacrifices, and this has been clarified in the translation.

rashi.heb:
*וירא ה' אל שלמה בלילה.* 
בחזיון לילה:
rashi.eng: *And the Lord appeared to Solomon at night.* in a vision of the night.

rashi.heb:
*שמעתי את תפלתך.* 
בלשון שאמר שלמה ושמעת השיב הקב"ה שמעתי תפלתך הוא התפלל בהעצר השמים השיב הקב"ה הן אעצור, הוא התפלל רעב וארבה והקב"ה משיבו והן אצוה על חגב, הוא התפלל על דבר והקב"ה משיבו ואם אשלח דבר בעמי ויכנעו עמי במה שיתפללו ויבקשו פני וישובו מדרכיהם הרעים הרי ג' כנגד ג':
rashi.eng: *I have heard your prayer.* With the wording that Solomon used, “And You shall hear.” The Holy One, blessed be He, answered him: “I have heard your prayer.” He prayed, (above 6:26): “When heaven is closed up.” And the Holy One, blessed be He, answered him, “If I close up.” He prayed concerning famine and locusts, and the Holy One, blessed be He, answered him, “if I command locusts.” He prayed concerning pestilence, and the Holy One, blessed be He, answered him, “or if I send pestilence upon My people, and My people… humble themselves” by praying and seeking My presence and repenting of their evil ways. Hence we have three [responses] corresponding to three [entreaties].

notes.224: (tn): Or “heavens.” The Hebrew term שָׁמַיִם (shamayim) may be translated “heaven(s)” or “sky” depending on the context.
notes.225: (tn, Heb): “the land,” which stands here by metonymy for the vegetation growing in it.

rashi.heb:
*הן אעצור.* 
והן אצוה ואם אשלח כנגד ג' תפילות ואני אשמע ואסלח לחטאתם וארפא את ארצם:
rashi.eng: *If I shut up… if I command… or if I send.* corresponding to three prayers, “I shall hear… and forgive their sin, and heal their land.”

notes.226: (tn, Heb): “over whom my name is called.” The Hebrew idiom “call the name over” indicates ownership. See 2 Sam 12:28.
notes.227: (tn, Heb): “seek my face,” where “my face” is figurative for God’s presence and acceptance.
notes.228: (tn, Heb): “and turn from their sinful ways.”
notes.230: (sn): Here the phrase heal their land means restore the damage done by the drought, locusts and plague mentioned in v. 13.

notes.231: (tn, Heb): “my eyes will be open and my ears attentive to the prayer of this place.” Note Solomon’s request in 6:40.

notes.232: (tn, Heb): “for my name to be there perpetually [or perhaps, “forever”].”
notes.233: (tn, Heb): “and my eyes and my heart will be there all the days.”

rashi.heb:
*והיו עיני ולבי.* 
תרגם יונתן ותהי שכינתי שריא ביה אם רעותי מתעבדא תמן כל יומיא, והיו עיני שם אם לבי וחפצי שם:
rashi.eng: *and My eyes and heart will be.* Jonathan renders (I Kings 9:3): “and My presence will rest there if My will is performed there at all times.” My eyes will be there if My heart and My will are there.

notes.234: (tn, Heb): “As for you, if you walk before me, as David your father walked, by doing all which I commanded you, [and] you keep my rules and my regulations.” Verse 17 is actually a lengthy protasis (“if” section) of a conditional sentence, the apodosis (“then” section) of which appears in v. 18.

notes.235: (tn, Heb): “I will establish the throne of your kingdom.”
notes.236: (tn, Heb): “there will not be cut off from you a man ruling over Israel.”

notes.237: (tn): The Hebrew pronoun is plural, suggesting that Solomon and all Israel (or perhaps Solomon and his successors) are in view. To convey this to the English reader, the translation “you people” has been employed.
notes.239: (tn, Heb): “and walk and serve other gods and bow down to them.”

notes.240: (tn, Heb): “them.” The switch from the second to the third person pronoun is rhetorically effective, for it mirrors God’s rejection of his people – he has stopped addressing them as “you” and begun addressing them as “them.” However, the switch is awkward and confusing in English, so the translation maintains the direct address style.
notes.241: (tn, Heb): “them.” See the note on “you” earlier in this verse.
notes.242: (tc, Heb): Instead of “I will throw away,” the parallel text in 1 Kgs 9:7 has “I will send away.” The two verbs sound very similar in Hebrew, so the discrepancy is likely due to an oral transmissional error. “and this temple which I consecrated for my name I will throw away from before my face.”
notes.243: (tn, Heb): “him,” which appears in context to refer to Israel (i.e., “you” in direct address). Many translations understand the direct object of the verb “make” to be the temple (NEB, NASB, NIV, NRSV “it”).
notes.244: (tn, Heb): “and I will make him [i.e., Israel] a proverb and a taunt,” that is, a proverbial example of destruction and an object of reproach.

rashi.heb:
*אשליך מעל פני.* 
כתנאי שביני וביניכם ואם לא תשמעו לי (ויקרא כ״ו:י״ד) מה נאמר והשימותי את מקדשיכם:
rashi.eng: *I shall cast from before Me.* according to the condition between Me and you, viz. (Lev. 26:14): “But if you do not heed Me.” What does it say there? (verse 31): “And I shall make your sanctuaries desolate.”

rashi.heb:
*ואתננו למשל ולשנינה.* 
כענין שמושלים משל על מי שאירע לו דבר פגע:
rashi.eng: *and I shall make it a proverb.* as people compose a proverb about someone who was befallen by misfortune.

rashi.heb:
*ולשנינה.* 
כמו (דברים ו׳:ז׳) ושננתם לבנך ותתנינון לשון סיפור רעות וכן תרגום ויספר ואשתעי ולשועי:
rashi.eng: *and a byword.* Heb. וְלִשְׁנִינָה, like (Deut. 6:7): וְשִׁנַּנְתָּם לְבָנֶיךָ, “and you shall teach them.” [It is] an expression of recounting misfortunes. Similarly, the Targum of (Gen. 37:10) וַיְסַפֵּר“And he told,” is וְאִשְׁתָּעֵי, and [the Targum of] וְלִשְׁנִינָה is וּלְשׁוּעֵי.

notes.245: (tn, Heb): “and this house which was high/elevated.” The statement makes little sense in this context, which predicts the desolation that judgment will bring. Some treat the clause as concessive, “Even though this temple is lofty [now].” Others, following the lead of several ancient versions, emend the text to, “this temple will become a heap of ruins.”

rashi.heb:
*לכל עובר עליו ישום.* 
כלומר יחרב הבית ואז כל עובר עליו ישום כמו (איוב י"ח) על יומו נשמו אחרונים:
rashi.eng: *every passerby will be astounded.* i.e., The Temple will be destroyed, and every passerby will then be astounded (יִשֹּׁם), like (Job 18:20): “Concerning his day - the later people shall be astonished (נָשַׁמּוּ).”

rashi.heb:
*במה עשה ה'.* 
כמו על מה עשה ה' (דברים כ"ט) וכן כתיב (במלכים א' ט'):
rashi.eng: *Why has the Lord done.* בַּמֶּה, like (Deut. 29:23): “Why (עַל מֶה) has the Lord done thus,” and so it is written in I Kings (9:9).

notes.248: (tn, Heb): “and they took hold of other gods and bowed down to them and served them.”

rashi.heb:
*ויהי מקץ עשרים שנה.* 
פתרון מקץ עשרים שנה שנגמר כל הבנין של בית ה' שבע שנים ואת ביתו י"ג שנים כדכתיב במלכים (שם ו):
rashi.eng: *Now it came to pass at the end of twenty years.* The meaning is: at the end of twenty years that the entire construction had been completed: that of the House of the Lord seven years and that of his palace thirteen years, as it is written in I Kings (6:38, 7:1).

notes.249: (tn, Heb): “Huram” (also in v. 18). Some medieval Hebrew mss, along with the LXX, Syriac, and Vulgate spell the name “Hiram,” agreeing with 1 Chr 14:1. “Huram” is a variant spelling referring to the same individual.

rashi.heb:
*ויבן את תדמור במדבר.* 
(ובמלכים א ט׳:י״ח) כתיב את תמור ותדמור קרינן וזה ששנינו ביבמות אין מקבלים גרים מן התרמודים ובב"ר בפרשת עקידה מפרש שעזרו לשונאיהם של ישראל ולפי שהמירו עצמם ונתחלפו לרעה בסוף על כן נכתב במלכים תמור לשון תמורה שהיה להם לעשות לישראל חסד עשה עמהם שלמה שבנה להם כרך תדמור ומשום שלמה לא נכתב כאן תמור אלא תדמור כלומר עיר חשובה הכל לכבוד שלמה שאין כבוד שלמה לומר כאן הא בנה כרך שמרדו בו וקלקלו בו ועל כן כתב תדמור ולא תמור:
rashi.eng: *And he built Tadmor in the desert.* In I Kings (9:18) it [the name] is written “Tamar,” but read, “Tadmor.” This accounts for that which we learned in Tractate Jebamoth (16a): We may not accept proselytes from the Tarmodites; and in Genesis Rabbah (56:11), in the portion dealing with the binding [of Isaac] it is explained that they aided Israel’s enemies, and because they changed themselves and became worse, the word תָּמָר is used in Kings, an expression of exchange (תְּמוּרָה), for they should have repaid Israel for the kindness that Solomon bestowed upon them, for he built the city of Tadmor for them. Because of Solomon, it is not written here “Tamar,” but “Tadmor,” i.e., an important city, in deference to Solomon’s honor, for it is no honor to Solomon to say here that he built a city which rebelled against him and sinned against him. Therefore, it is written, “Tadmor,” and not “Tamar.”

notes.250: (tn, Heb): “and he built…[as] cities of fortification, [with] walls, doors, and a bar.”

rashi.heb:
*ערי מצור.* 
לפי שהיו עומדים על התחום הוצרכו חוזק כל כך:
rashi.eng: *fortified cities.* Because they stood on the border, they needed to be fortified.

notes.251: (tn, Heb): “Solomon.” The recurrence of the proper name is unexpected in terms of contemporary English style, so the pronoun has been used in the translation instead.
notes.252: (tn, Heb): “the cities of the chariots and the cities of the horses.”
notes.253: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
notes.254: (tn, Heb): “and all the desire of Solomon which he desired to build in Jerusalem and in Lebanon and in all the land of his kingdom.”

notes.255: (tn, Heb): “all the people who were left from the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, who were not from Israel.”

notes.256: (tn, Heb): “from their sons who were left after them in the land, whom the sons of Israel did not wipe out, and Solomon raised them up for a work crew to this day.”

notes.257: (tn, Heb): “and from the sons of Israel which Solomon did not assign to the laborers for his work.”
notes.258: (tn, Heb): “officers of his chariots and his horses.”

rashi.heb:
*למלאכתו.* 
למלאכת בניינו למה כי הגרים למלאכתו ולא אנשי ישראל לפי כי ישראל המה אנשי חיל ואנשי מלחמה ושרי רכבו ופרשיו:
rashi.eng: *for his work.* [i.e.] for the work of his building. Why? All the proselytes were [employed] to do his work, but not the men of Israel, because the Israelites served as soldiers and men of war and the officers of his chariots and his horsemen.

notes.259: (tn, Heb): “these [were] the officials of the governors who belonged to the king, Solomon, 250, the ones ruling over the people.”

rashi.heb:
*חמשים ומאתי'.* 
ובמלכים (א' ט') חמשים וחמש מאות אלא זה וזה אחד הוא שמחסר לשם ג' מאות ושנה ומנה אותם שוב שהרי שם כתוב למעלה לבד משרי הנצבים וגו' שלשת אלפים ושלש מאות הרודים וכאן כתיב לעיל שלשת אלפים ושש מאות נמצא מה שחסר בפסוק אחד הוסיף בפסוק אחר ומחלקם בשביל שהג' מאות היתרים גרים היו והיו ממונים על אותן ג' אלפים וג' מאות הרודים על ע' אלף נשא סבל ופ' אלף חצב בהר ואלו חמשים ומאתים הנאמר כאן ישראלים היו ממונים על אותם ג' מאות גרים:
rashi.eng: *two hundred fifty.* And in I Kings (9:23): “five hundred fifty,” but [in fact], these two are identical, for there Scripture deducts three hundred and then repeats and counts them again, for there it is written (5:30): “Besides Solomon’s chief officers, etc….three thousand and three hundred, who bore rule,” and here it is written above (2:1): “three thousand six hundred.” We find that what is missing in one verse is added in the other verse. Scripture separates them because the three hundred extra were proselytes, and they were appointed over those three thousand three hundred who ruled over the seventy thousand who bore burdens and the eighty thousand hewers in the mountains (I Kings 5:29), and these two hundred fifty were Israelites, appointed over those three hundred proselytes.

notes.260: (sn): The phrase the City of David refers here to the fortress of Zion in Jerusalem, not to Bethlehem. See 2 Sam 5:7.

rashi.heb:
*העלה שלמה מעיר דוד.* 
היא ציון שהושיבה בעיר דוד כשלקחה והיתה שם עד כלותו לבנות את ביתו:
rashi.eng: *Solomon brought up from the City of David.* That is Zion, for he let her dwell in the City of David when he married her, and she was there until he completed building his palace.

rashi.heb:
*כי קדש המה.* 
כל העיר וכל הבתים:
rashi.eng: *because they are holy.* The entire city and all the houses.

rashi.heb:
*אשר באה אליהם.* 
לפי שבאה אליהם ארון ה' באה לשון נקבה דוגמא (שמואל א ד׳:ג׳) וארון ברית ה' נלקחה:
rashi.eng: *since the Ark of the Lord came to them.* because the Ark of the Lord had come to them. [The word] בָּאָה is a feminine expression, similar to (I Sam. 4:17): “and the Ark of the Covenant of the Lord (sic) was taken (נִלְקְחָה).”

rashi.heb:
*על מזבח ה'.* 
זה מזבח הנחשת שבנה שלמה וי"מ מזבח הנחשת שעשה שלמה תחת מזבח הנחשת שבנה משה ותימה בדבר שהרי כתיב (מלכים ב' י"ז) ואת עולת כל עם וכל דם עולה וגו' יהיה לבקר כלומר מזבח הנחשת שהיה שם קודם לכן יהיה לי לבקר מכלל שהמזבח היה של נחושת:
rashi.eng: *on the altar of the Lord.* This was the copper altar that Solomon built. Some explain that this was the copper altar that Solomon made instead of the copper altar that Moses built, but this is astounding, because it is written (II Kings 16:15): “and the burnt offerings of the entire people of the land, etc. and the blood of every burnt offering, etc. shall be for me to visit,” i.e., the copper altar, which was there heretofore, shall be for me to visit. This proves that Moses’ copper altar was still there.

notes.262: (tn): The Hebrew phrase הַסֻּכּוֹת[חַג] (khag hassukot, “[festival of] huts” [or “shelters”]) is traditionally known as the Feast of Tabernacles. The rendering “booths” (cf. NAB, NASB, NRSV) is probably better than the traditional “tabernacles” in light of the meaning of the term סֻכָּה (sukkah, “hut; booth”), but “booths” are frequently associated with trade shows and craft fairs in contemporary American English. The nature of the celebration during this feast as a commemoration of the wanderings of the Israelites after they left Egypt suggests that a translation like “temporary shelters” is more appropriate.

notes.263: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Solomon) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.264: (tn, Heb): “and the Levites, according to their posts, to praise and to serve opposite the priests according to the matter of a day in its day.”
notes.265: (tn, Heb): “and the gatekeepers by their divisions for a gate and a gate.”
notes.266: (tn, Heb): “for so [was] the command of David the man of God.”

notes.267: (tn, Heb): “and they did not turn aside from the command of the king concerning the priests and the Levites with regard to any matter and with regard to the treasuries.”

rashi.heb:
*עד היום מוסד בית.* 
מיום הוסדו עד כלותו:
rashi.eng: *until this day [from] the founding of the House of the Lord.* From the day of its founding until its completion.

notes.268: (tn, Heb): “and Huram sent to him by the hand of his servants, ships, and servants [who] know the sea, and they came with the servants of Solomon to Ophir.”
notes.269: (tn): The Hebrew word כִּכַּר (kikar, “circle”) refers generally to something that is round. When used of metals it can refer to a disk-shaped weight made of the metal or, by extension, to a standard unit of weight. According to the older (Babylonian) standard the “talent” weighed 130 lbs. (58.9 kg), but later this was lowered to 108.3 lbs. (49.1 kg). More recent research suggests the “light” standard talent was 67.3 lbs. (30.6 kg). Using this as the standard for calculation, the weight of the gold was 30,285 lbs. (13,770 kg).

notes.272: (tn, Heb): “Solomon.” The recurrence of the proper name here is redundant in terms of contemporary English style, so the pronoun has been used in the translation instead.
notes.274: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
notes.275: (tn, Heb): “with very great strength.” The Hebrew word חַיִל (khayil, “strength”) may refer here to the size of her retinue or to the great wealth she brought with her.

rashi.heb:
*לנסות את שלמה.* 
אם אמת מה ששמעה מחכמתו ובאה לנסותו:
rashi.eng: *to test Solomon.* whether that which she had heard about his wisdom was true, and she came to test him.

rashi.heb:
*בחידות.* 
כמו (שופטים י״ד:י״ב) אחודה נא לכם חידה דשמשון:
rashi.eng: *with riddles.* like (Jud. 14:12): “Let me ask you a riddle [in the story] of Samson.

notes.277: (tn, Heb): “Solomon declared to her all her words; there was not a word hidden from the king which he did not declare to her.” If riddles are specifically in view (see v. 1), then one might translate, “Solomon explained to her all her riddles; there was no riddle too complex for the king.”

rashi.heb:
*ולא נעלם דבר.* 
כיון שראתה שהגיד לה הכל לא נעלם דבר ממה ששאלה אשר הגיד לה אז הודתה על השמועה כי אמת שמעה ובתרגום מגלת אסתר שם כתובים קצת מן החידות אשר שאלתו:
rashi.eng: *and nothing was hidden.* Since she saw that he told her everything, and nothing that she asked him was hidden, she admitted that the report she had heard was true. In the Targum (Sheni) of Megillath Esther (1:2), some of the riddles that she asked him are written.

notes.281: (tn, Heb): “the seating of his servants and the standing of his attendants.”
notes.282: (tc): The Hebrew text has here, “and his upper room [by] which he was going up to the house of the Lord.” But עֲלִיָּתוֹ (’aliyyato, “his upper room”) should be emended to עֹלָתוֹ, (’olato, “his burnt sacrifice[s]”). See the parallel account in 1 Kgs 10:5.
notes.283: (tn, Heb): Or “it took her breath away”; “there was no breath still in her.”

rashi.heb:
*ומאכל שלחנו.* 
ברבורים ומיני מעדנים העולים על שלחנו לרוב:
rashi.eng: *And the food of his table.* fowl (I Kings 5:3) and kinds of delicacies that were served on his table in abundance.

rashi.heb:
*ומושב עבדיו.* 
שכל אחד ואחד היה מכיר את מקומו כשהיו יושבים על השולחן ורואי פני המלך תדיר לא היה א' רשאי לישב במקום חבירו כל ימי חייו:
rashi.eng: *and the seating of his servants.* That each one recognized his place when they were seated at the table, and of those who constantly saw the king’s face, no one was allowed to sit in his neighbor’s place all the days of his life.

rashi.heb:
*ומעמד משרתיו.* 
כל אחד ואחד היה מחזיק במעמד שלו ובשירות שלו ולא היה משנה למחר:
rashi.eng: *and the seating of his servants.*  Each one would retain his station and his position, and he would not change it the next day.

rashi.heb:
*ומלבושיהם.* 
לא כמלבושיהם שהם לבושים היום לובשים למחר:
rashi.eng: *and their attire.*  The attire that they would wear tomorrow was not the same as, the attire that they wore today.

rashi.heb:
*ומשקיו.* 
רוב משקיו:
rashi.eng: *and his cupbearers.*  most of his cupbearers.

rashi.heb:
*ועליתו.* 
מסלות עליותיו אשר יעלה עליהם מביתו לבית ה':
rashi.eng: *and his ascent.*  the stairway by which he ascended from his palace to the Temple.

rashi.heb:
*ולא היה עוד בה רוח.* 
שהיתה סבורה שאין חכמה בכל המלכיות כי אם בארצה וכמו חכמיה כי ארצה במזרח ולפיכך הם חכמים ביותר לפי שמסתכלין במזלות כדאיתא בפרק קמא דראש השנה לדידן מכסי סיהרא י"ח שעו' דארץ ישראל במערב בבל וזהו שכתוב ותרב חכמת שלמה מכל חכמת בני קדם שהם היו במזרח כדכתיב ויהי בנסע' מקדם (בראשית י"א) ומכל חכמת מצרים שהיו מכשפים חרטומים ואשפים וחכם היה בטיי"ר כך כתיב בפסיקתא טייר הוא ל' ערבי ובויקרא רבה בפ' בן המצרי כי עוף השמים יוליך את הקול (קהלת) זה עורב וחכמת טויארי:
rashi.eng: *and she was breathless.* because she thought that there was no wisdom in any of the kingdoms but in her own country and like that of her wise men, because her country was in the east; they were wise because they were stargazers, as is stated in the first chapter of Tractate Rosh Hashanah, for Eretz Israel is west of Babylon, and that is what is written (I Kings 5:10): “And Solomon’s wisdom was greater than the wisdom of all the children of the east,” for they were in the east, as it is written (Gen. 11:2): “And it came to pass as they migrated from the east.” (I Kings 5:10) “And all the wisdom of Egypt,” for they were sorcerers, necromancers, and astrologers, and he was wise in divination (tayer). So it is written in Pesikta (d’Rav Kahana p. 33b). The word (tayer) is Arabic, and in Leviticus Rabbah (32:2), in the chapter dealing with the son of the Egyptian (24:10): (Eccl. 10:20): “for a bird of the air shall carry the voice.” This is the raven and refers to the art of bird divination.

notes.284: (tn, Heb): “about your words [or perhaps, “deeds”] and your wisdom.”

notes.285: (tn, Heb): “the half was not told to me.”

rashi.heb:
*חצי מרבית.* 
רבוי חכמות:
rashi.eng: *half of your abundant [wisdom].*  The many wisdoms

notes.286: (tn, Heb): “How happy are your men! How happy are these servants of yours, who stand before you continually, who hear your wisdom!”

notes.288: (tn, Heb): “as king for the Lord your God.”

notes.291: (tn): The Hebrew word כִּכַּר (kikar, “circle”) refers generally to something that is round. When used of metals it can refer to a disk-shaped weight made of the metal or, by extension, to a standard unit of weight. According to the older (Babylonian) standard the “talent” weighed 130 lbs. (58.9 kg), but later this was lowered to 108.3 lbs. (49.1 kg). More recent research suggests the “light” standard talent was 67.3 lbs. (30.6 kg). Using this as the standard for calculation, the weight of the gold was 8,076 lbs. (3,672 kg).
notes.292: (tn, Heb): “there has not been like those spices which the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.”

notes.293: (tn, Heb): “Huram’s” (also in v. 21). Some medieval Hebrew mss, along with the LXX, Syriac, and Vulgate spell the name “Hiram,” agreeing with 1 Chr 14:1. “Huram” is a variant spelling referring to the same individual.
notes.294: (tn, Heb): “who brought gold from Ophir, brought.”

rashi.heb:
*עצי אלגומים.* 
מפרש בפסיקת' כתוב אחד אומר אלמוגים וכתוב אחד אומר אלגומים אלא אלגומים שמם ונקרא אלמוגים לפי שהיה מתמוגג ונכפף מתוך רכיכתו כמו כוסות שהוא נכפף מתוך חשיבתו:
rashi.eng: *algom wood .*  In Pesikta it is explained: One verse (I Kings 10:11) says אלמוגים, and one verse says אלגומים. The truth is that its name is אלגומים, but it is called אלמוגים because it melted and bent because of its softness, (like cups, which bend because of their value.)

notes.296: (tn, Heb): “tracks.” The parallel text in 1 Kgs 10:12 has a different term whose meaning is uncertain: “supports,” perhaps “banisters” or “parapets.”
notes.297: (tn): Two types of stringed instruments are specifically mentioned in the Hebrew text, the כִּנּוֹר (kinnor, “zither”) and נֶבֶל (nevel, “harp”).
notes.298: (tn, Heb): “there was not seen like these formerly in the land of Judah.”

rashi.heb:
*מסלות.* 
מדרגות (ובמלכים א' י') כתיב מסעד כדרך שעושין לעולין בדרך מעלות ומדרגות וי"א מסעד ומסילה אחד הם:
rashi.eng: *stairs .* In I Kings (10:12) it is written מסעד, [a support] after the manner that they make for those who ascend by way of elevated places and stairs. Some say that מסעד and ומסילה are one and the same.

rashi.heb:
*וכנרות ונבלים לשרים.* 
י"א לבני לוי המשוררים בכלי שיר ור' אליעזר זצ"ל פי' לשרים המשוררים לטייל לפני המלך דוגמא (שם ד') ויהי שירו חמשה ואלף הם שירות של חול שעשה לשורר לפניו לטייל והוא שכתוב (לקמן ל"ה) ויקונן ירמיה על יאשיהו ויאמרו כל השרים והשרות וגו':
rashi.eng: *and harps and psalteries for the singers .* Some say (Jonathan and Rashi to Kings) for the Levites who sing with musical instruments, and Rabbi Eliezer explained it to mean: for the singers who stroll before the king. A similar case is (I Kings 5:12): “and his songs were a thousand and five.” These were secular songs that he composed to sing before him, and that is what is meant (below 35:25): “And Jeremiah lamented over Josiah, and all the male singers and the female singers recited in their lamentations, etc.”

notes.299: (tn, Heb): “besides what she brought to the king.”

rashi.heb:
*מלבד אשר הביאה.* 
משום כבוד מלכי יהודה כתיב כאן דמשמע שהיא נתנה לו יותר ממה שנתן לה ובמלכים (שם י) כתיב מלבד אשר נתן לה כיד המלך דברים המצויין בא"י ואינם מצויין במקומ':
rashi.eng: *aside from that which she brought.* This is written here in deference to the honor of the kings of Judah; it means that she gave him more than he gave her, and in I Kings (10:13) it is written: “aside from that which he gave her according to King [Solomon’s] ability.” [He gave her] things that were common in the land of Israel, but were not common in her country.

notes.301: (tn): The Hebrew word כִּכַּר (kikar, “circle”) refers generally to something that is round. When used of metals it can refer to a disk-shaped weight made of the metal or, by extension, to a standard unit of weight. According to the older (Babylonian) standard the “talent” weighed 130 lbs. (58.9 kg), but later this was lowered to 108.3 lbs. (49.1 kg). More recent research suggests the “light” standard talent was 67.3 lbs. (30.6 kg). Using this as the standard for calculation, the weight of the gold Solomon received annually was 44,822 lbs. (20,380 kg).
notes.302: (tn, Heb): “the weight of the gold which came to Solomon in one year was 666 units of gold.”

rashi.heb:
*לבד מאנשי התרים.* 
שהיו דואגים לעבור ממדינה למדינה וממלכו' למלכות בלא תייר והיו נותנים לו שכר תייר:
rashi.eng: *Aside from that which the guides.* They were afraid to pass from province to province or from kingdom to kingdom without a guide, and they would give him the guide’s fee.

rashi.heb:
*והסוחרים מביאים.* 
שהיו מביאי' לו ע"י עלילה כדי לראות חכמתו:
rashi.eng: *and the merchants would bring.* They would bring him [gold] on a pretext in order to see his wisdom.
*and all the kings of Arabia.* the kings of the Arabians.
*and the regents of the land.* They would all bring [gold and silver] in order to see his wisdom.

notes.304: (tn): The Hebrew text has simply “600,” with no unit of measure given.

rashi.heb:
*מאתים צנה.* 
צנה מקפת את האדם משלש רוחותיו הוא שכת' (תהילים ה׳:י״ג) כצנה רצון תעטרנו:
rashi.eng: *Aside from that which the guides.* which encompasses the person from his three sides, as is written (Ps. 5:13): “As a shield You encompass him with favor”.

rashi.heb:
*זהב שחוט.* 
זהב רך ונוח להרקע מרוב חשיבותו שנטוה כחוט:
rashi.eng: *malleable gold.* They would bring him [gold] on a pretext in order to see his wisdom.

rashi.heb:
*שש מאות זהב.* 
שש מאות זהובים והוא שש מנים שהזהב הוא הדינר:
rashi.eng: *a gold that is soft and easily flattened out..* six hundred zehubim, the equivalent of six manehs, for the zahab is the dinar.

notes.305: (tn): The Hebrew text has simply “300,” with no unit of measure given.
notes.306: (sn): This name was appropriate because of the large amount of cedar, undoubtedly brought from Lebanon, used in its construction. The cedar pillars in the palace must have given it the appearance of a forest. See 1 Kgs 7:2.

rashi.heb:
*יער הלבנון.* 
בית גדול בנה שלמה בירושלים כדמוכח לקמן וכל אותם מגיני' לקח שישק ומריבוי עצי הלבנון הגדולים עשאן כדכתיב במלכים (א' ז') ויבן את בית יער הלבנון על ארבע טורי ארזים ושם נתן אותם מגינים והוא שכתוב ותבט ביום ההוא אל נשק בית היער (ישעיהו כ״ב:ח׳):
rashi.eng: *the forest of Lebanon.* Solomon built a huge house in Jerusalem, as is proven further, and Shishak took all those shields (below 12:9), and he made them (sic) from an abundance of the large trees of Lebanon, as it is written in I Kings (7:2): “And he built the house of the forest of Lebanon, etc. on four rows, etc.,” and there he deposited those shields, and that is what is written (Isa. 22:8): “and you looked on that day to the weapons of the house of the forest.”

rashi.heb:
*כסא שן.* 
שן של פיל:
rashi.eng: *ivory throne.* the ivory of elephants.

notes.307: (tc): The parallel text of 1 Kgs 10:19 has instead “and the back of it was rounded on top.”
notes.308: (tn, Heb): “[There were] armrests on each side of the place of the seat, and two lions standing beside the armrests.”

rashi.heb:
*ושש מעלות לכסא.* 
מדרגות לעלות בו:
rashi.eng: *And there were six steps to the throne.* steps by which to ascend.

rashi.heb:
*וידות מזה ומזה על מקום השבת.* 
כמין מקלות מפאה לפאה מימין ומשמאל ולסמוך זרועותיו עליהם:
rashi.eng: *with armrests on either side by the place of the seat.* like rods from corner to corner, from the right and from the left, upon which to support his arms.

rashi.heb:
*ושנים אריות עומדים אצל הידות.* 
של זהב וכל צורת הכסא וצורת החיות שבכסא מפורש בתרגום של מגילת אסתר:
rashi.eng: *and two lions were standing beside the armrests .*  [The lions were made] of gold, and the entire form of the throne and the forms of the beasts that were in the throne are depicted in the Targum of the Scroll of Esther (1:2).

notes.309: (tn, Heb): “nothing like it had been made for any kingdom.”

rashi.heb:
*ושנים אריות עומדים אצל הידות.* 
של זהב וכל צורת הכסא וצורת החיות שבכסא מפורש בתרגום של מגילת אסתר:
rashi.eng: *and two lions were standing beside the armrests.* [The lions were made] of gold, and the entire form of the throne and the forms of the beasts that were in the throne are depicted in the Targum of the Scroll of Esther (1:2).

notes.310: (tn, Heb): “there was no silver, it was not regarded as anything in the days of Solomon.”

notes.311: (tn, Heb): “for ships belonging to the king were going [to] Tarshish with the servants of Huram.” This probably refers to large ships either made in or capable of traveling to the distant western port of Tarshish.
notes.314: (tn, Heb): “the ships of Tarshish came carrying.”
notes.315: (tn): The meaning of this word is unclear; some suggest it refers to “baboons.” NEB has “monkeys,” NASB, NRSV “peacocks,” and NIV “baboons.”

rashi.heb:
*שנהבים.* 
שן פיל ופיל עצמו:
rashi.eng: *ivory.* the tusks of elephants and the elephants themselves.

rashi.heb:
*וקופים.* 
מע"ר קאצ"ן:
rashi.eng: *and apes.* In German, meerkats, long-tailed monkeys.

rashi.heb:
*ותוכיים.* 
טווסין:
rashi.eng: *and peackocks.*  Heb. tavsin

notes.316: (tn, Heb): “King Solomon was greater than all the kings of the earth with respect to wealth and wisdom.”

rashi.heb:
*ויגדל המלך שלמה וגו'.* 
לקיים מה שאמר לו וגם אשר לא שאלת אתן לך גם כבוד (מלכים א ג׳:י״ג):
rashi.eng: *Now King Solomon transcended etc..* To fulfill that which He said to him, (I Kings 3:13): “And I have also given you that which you have not asked, etc. and honor.”

notes.317: (tn, Heb): “and all the kings of the earth were seeking the face of Solomon to hear his wisdom which God had placed in his heart.”

rashi.heb:
*וכל מלכי הארץ וגו'.* 
לקיים מה שאמר לו הנה נתתי לך לב חכם ונבון אשר כמוך לא יהיה (שם):
rashi.eng: *And all the kings of the Earth, etc..* To fulfill that which He said to him, (ibid. verse 12): “Behold I have given you a wise and understanding heart; so that there was none like you before you.”

notes.318: (tn, Heb): “and they were bringing each one his gift, items of silver…and mules, the matter of a year in a year.”

rashi.heb:
*והם מביאים איש מנחתו.* 
על ידי עלילה שבאים לשמוע חכמתו כי אין כבוד לבוא לפני המלך ריקם, דוגמת ולא יראה את פני ה' ריקם (דברים ט״ז:ט״ז):
rashi.eng: *And each one would bring his gift.* as a pretext because they were [really] coming to hear [his wisdom], since it is disrespectful to come before a king empty-handed, similar to (Deut. 16:16): “and he shall not appear before the Lord empty-handed.”

rashi.heb:
*נשק.* 
כלי זיין:
rashi.eng: *weapons.* armaments

notes.319: (tc): The parallel text of 1 Kgs 10:26 reads “fourteen hundred chariots.”
notes.320: (tn, Heb): “he placed them in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.” For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

rashi.heb:
*ויניחם בערי הרכב ועם המלך בירושלים.* 
מקצתם ועבר על לא ירבה לו סוסים:
rashi.eng: *and he placed them in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem..* some of them. He transgressed [the negative commandment of] (Deut. 17:17): “Only he shall not multiply horses to himself.”

notes.321: (tn, Heb): “the River.” In biblical Hebrew the Euphrates River was typically referred to simply as “the River.”

notes.322: (tn): The words “as plentiful” are supplied for clarification.
notes.324: (tn, Heb): “as the sycamore fig trees which are in the Shephelah.”

notes.325: (tn, Heb): “As for the rest of the events of Solomon, the former and the latter, are they not written?”

rashi.heb:
*על דברי נתן.* 
ויהי בלילה ההוא ויהי דבר ה' אל נתן וגומר (שמואל ב י״ב:כ״ה) עד ויקרא שמו ידידיה:
rashi.eng: *in the words of Nathan the prophet.* (II Sam. 12:25): “And He sent by the hand of Nathan the prophet, and he called his name Jedidiah for the Lord’s sake.”

rashi.heb:
*ועל נבואת אחיה השילוני.* 
(מלכים א י״א:כ״ט) שקרע ממנו המלכות ונתנה לירבעם:
rashi.eng: *and in the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite.* (I Kings 11:31) who rent the kingdom from him and gave it to Jeroboam.

notes.326: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

rashi.heb:
*על כל ישראל ארבעים שנה.* 
מה שאין כן בדוד שבחברון מלך ז' שנים ובירושלים שלשים ושלש:
rashi.eng: *over all Israel forty years.*  unlike David, who reigned seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem.

notes.329: (tn, Heb): “him”; the referent (Rehoboam) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*כי שכם באו כל ישראל להמליך אותו.* 
בשכם שהוא מקום ירבעם שבחלק אפרים וירבעם אפרתי וכל זאת היתה סיבה מאת הקדוש ברוך הוא לקיים דברו קרוע אקרע הממלכה:
rashi.eng: *for all Israel had come to Shechem to make him king.* In Shechem, which was Jeroboam’s place, which was in the territory of Ephraim. And Jeroboam was an Ephrathite, and all this was brought about by the Holy One, blessed be He, to fulfill His word, (I Kings 11:11): “I will surely tear the kingdom.”

rashi.heb:
*ויהי כשמוע.* 
פתרון ויהי כשמוע מקודם לכן שבאו להמליכו בשכם כשהוא עודנו במצרים:
rashi.eng: *And it was when… heard.* The meaning is: And it was when he heard - prior to this, when they came to make him [Rehoboam] king in Shechem, when he [Jeroboam] was still in Egypt.

notes.330: (tn, Heb): “They sent and called for him.”

rashi.heb:
*וישלחו ויקראו לו ויבא.* 
וכל זה להודיענו רצונו של מלך מלכי המלכים הקב"ה שאפילו ירבעם עצמו בא להמליכו לרחבעם והסב הקב"ה אחר דבריו עד שמלך ירבעם:
rashi.eng: *And they sent and called him, and… came.* All this was to let us know the will of the Holy One, blessed be He, that even Jeroboam himself came to make Rehoboam king, but the Holy One, blessed be He, reversed his words [i.e., Jeroboam’s intention,] until Jeroboam reigned.

notes.332: (tn, Heb): “but you, now, lighten the burdensome work of your father and the heavy yoke which he placed on us, and we will serve you.” In the Hebrew text the prefixed verbal form with vav (וְנַעַבְדֶךָ, v�na’avdekha, “and we will serve you”) following the imperative (הָקֵל, haqel, “lighten”) indicates purpose/result. The conditional sentence used in the present translation is an attempt to bring out the logical relationship between these forms.

rashi.heb:
*אביך הקשה את עלנו.* 
כי איש טורח במלאכה היה ועלינו הטיל לפרנס פועליו והמס כדכתיב במלכים (א ה') ויעל המלך שלמה מס וגומר:
rashi.eng: *Your father made our yoke hard.* because he was a man who toiled at work, and he made it incumbent upon us to sustain his laborers with the tax, as it is written in I Kings (5:27): “And King Solomon raised a levy, etc.”

rashi.heb:
*נועצים.* 
כמו יועצים וכן יאמר מן יודעים נודעים אך יועצים להבא נועצים נתיעצים כבר:
rashi.eng: *How do you advise.* Heb. נוֹעָצִים, [in the passive voice], like יוֹעֲצִים [in the active voice], and so he says from יוֹדְעִים, נוֹדָעִים. יוֹעֲצִים means the future, and נוֹעָצִים means that which they already counseled.

notes.335: (tn, Heb): “If today you are for good to these people and you are favorable to them and speak to them good words, they will be your servants all the days.”

notes.336: (tn, Heb): “Rehoboam rejected the advice of the elders which they advised and he consulted the young men with whom he had grown up, who stood before him.”

notes.337: (tn, Heb): “Lighten the yoke which your father placed on us.”

notes.338: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Rehoboam) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.339: (tn, Heb): “Your father made our yoke heavy, but make it lighter upon us.”
notes.340: (tn, Heb): “My little one is thicker than my father’s hips.” The referent of “my little one” is not clear. The traditional view is that it refers to the little finger (so NEB, NASB, NIV, NRSV, NLT). As the following statement makes clear, Rehoboam’s point is that he is more harsh and demanding than his father.

rashi.heb:
*קטני עבה ממתני אבי.* 
אצבע קטנה שלי גדולה ממתני אבי כלומר אני חזק ממנו:
rashi.eng: *My little finger is thicker than my father’s loins.* My little finger is larger than my father’s loins; i.e., I am stronger than he.

notes.341: (tn, Heb): “and now my father placed upon you a heavy yoke, but I will add to your yoke.”
notes.342: (tn, Heb): “My father punished you with whips, but I [will punish you] with scorpions.” “Scorpions” might allude to some type of torture, but more likely it refers to a type of whip that inflicts an especially biting, painful wound.

rashi.heb:
*העמיס.* 
כמו (ראשית מ"ג) ויעמוס איש על חמורו:
rashi.eng: *burdened.* Heb. הֶעֱמִיס, loaded, like (Gen. 44:13): “and each man loaded (וַיַּעֲמס) his donkey.”

rashi.heb:
*בעקרבים.* 
ברימ"ן בל' אשכנ"ז שעוקצין כעקרבים:
rashi.eng: *with scorpions.* Brimmen in German, which sting like scorpions.

notes.343: (tn, Heb): “Rehoboam.” The pronoun “he” has been used in the translation in place of the proper name in keeping with contemporary English style.

notes.344: (tc): The Hebrew text reads, “I will make heavy your yoke,” but many medieval Hebrew mss and other ancient textual witnesses have, “my father made heavy your yoke.”
notes.345: (tn, Heb): “but I will add to your yoke.”
notes.346: (tn, Heb): “My father punished you with whips, but I [will punish you] with scorpions.” “Scorpions” might allude to some type of torture, but more likely it refers to a type of whip that inflicts an especially biting, painful wound.

notes.347: (tn, Heb): “because this turn of events was from God.”
notes.348: (tn, Heb): “so that the Lord might bring to pass his word which he spoke.”

rashi.heb:
*כי היתה נסבה.* 
למען הקים ה' את דברו כמו שמפורש (במלכים א יא) להסיר ממנו י' השבטים וליתן לירבעם וזהו לא יסור שבט מיהודה (ראשית מ"ט) לא ירד ממלכותו עד כי יבא שילה פתרון עד כי יבא יהודה שילה להמליך שם רחבעם ושם לו יקהת עמים להמליכו ושם נחלקה המלכות ואבד מלכות של עשר' השבטים ושכם עיר קטנה סמוכה לשילה כדכתיב (סוף שופטים) והנה חג לה' בשילה מימים ימימה במסילה העולה מבית אל שכמה וכתיב בירמיה משכם ומשילה ולכבוד משכן שילה נאספים לשכם שהוא ראוי לאסיפת בני אדם וסמוכה לשילה וכשנאספים בשכם אז יסור שבט מיהודה ששם המלכות נחלקה:
rashi.eng: *because it was brought about, etc. so that the Lord God might establish His word.* as is delineated in I Kings (11:31-37), to remove from him the ten tribes and to give them to Jeroboam, and this is the meaning of (Gen. 49:10): “The scepter will not depart from Judah” [meaning that] he will not be banished from his kingdom, “until he comes to Shiloh,” meaning until Judah comes to Shiloh to crown Rehoboam there, and there “peoples will gather to him” to crown him, and there the kingdom was divided, and the reign over the ten tribes was lost. Now Shechem is a small city adjacent to Shiloh, as it is written at the end of Judges (21:19): “Behold, there is a sacrifice before the Lord in Shiloh from time to time, etc. on the east side of the highway that goes up from Beth-El to Shechem,” and it is written in Jeremiah (41:5): “from Shechem (and) from Shiloh,” and in honor of the Tabernacle of Shiloh, they would gather in Shechem, which was fit for the people to assemble in, and it adjoined Shiloh. And when they would assemble in Shechem, the scepter would depart from Judah, for there the kingdom was divided.

notes.349: (sn): The people’s point seems to be that they have no familial relationship with David that brings them any benefits or places upon them any obligations. They are being treated like outsiders.
notes.350: (tn, Heb): “each one to your tents, Israel.” The word “return” is supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.

rashi.heb:
*לאהליך ישראל.* 
מוסב על מה לנו חלק בדוד מה לעזוב אהלינו ולילך אחריו לא כן אלא לכו כל ישראל איש לאהליו:
rashi.eng: *Each man to your homes, O Israel.* This refers back to, “What share do we have in David?” Why should we leave our homes and follow him? Not so, but all Israel, return each man to his home.

rashi.heb:
*עתה ראה ביתך דוד.* 
מוסב על ולא נחלה בבן ישי כלומר אין לנו בו נחלה אלא בבית המקדש שבירושלים שאנו זובחים בו ולראות בו בשלש רגלים:
rashi.eng: *Now see your house, David.* This refers back to, “And no heritage in Jesse’s son,” i.e., we have no heritage in him, but in the Temple in Jerusalem, where we sacrifice and appear on the three Pilgrimage Festivals.

rashi.heb:
*ראה ביתך דוד.* 
אין אנו צריכין לו לילך שם יהיה לך לבדך (וכל זה לא נראה לי) אלא ראה ביתך דוד אי איפשנו לא בך ולא בבית המקדש שלך:
rashi.eng: *see your house, David.* We do not need it to go there. Let it be yours alone. (But all this does not appeal to me) but, “See your house, David we have no desire either in you or in your Temple.”

notes.353: (sn): In the parallel account in 1 Kgs 12:18 this name appears as “Adoniram.”
notes.354: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

rashi.heb:
*הדורם.* 
הוא אדונירם (מלכים א' ד') שבימי שלמה גדולתו גדולה ובימי רחבעם נשפלה גדולתו על כן נקרא הדורם:
rashi.eng: *Hadoram.* He is identical with Adoniram (I Kings 4:6), for during Solomon’s time, he enjoyed great eminence, but in Rehoboam’s time his greatness was humbled. Therefore, he was called Hadoram.

rashi.heb:
*וירגמו בו בני ישראל אבן.* 
ולפי שרחבעם לא ידע הסבה והקשר שהסבו ממנו על כן נהרג כששאל המס שקצב עליהם שלמה:
rashi.eng: *and the Children of Israel pelted him with stones.* and because Rehoboam did not know the cause of the rebellion in which they turned away from him, he was slain when he requested the levy that Solomon had levied upon them.

rashi.heb:
*ויפשעו ישראל בבית דוד.* 
לשון מרדות ודוגמא (מלכים ב') בימיו פשע מואב וגו' (משלי י"א) את נפשע מקרית עוז, אז תפשע לבנה (לקמן ל"א):
rashi.eng: *And the Israelites rebelled against the house of David.* Heb. וַיִפְשְׁעוּ, an expression of rebellion. Examples are (II Kings 1:1): “Moab rebelled (וַיִפְשַׁע) against Israel;” (Prov. 18:19): “A rebellious (נִפְשַׁע) brother;” (below 27:19): “then Libnah rebelled (תִּפְשַׁע).”

notes.355: (tn, Heb): “he summoned the house of Judah and Benjamin, 180,000 chosen men, accomplished in war.”

rashi.heb:
*ויקהל את בית יהודה ובנימן.* 
שהיו בתחום יחד וגם ירושלים היתה של שניהם ובית המקדש על תחום שניהם בנוי ובגבולים ביהושע מפרש היאך היה תחומן יחד וגם רבותינו אמרו רצועה יוצאה מחלק בנימין ונכנסת בחלקו של יהודה ועליה מזבח בנוי לכך לא היו יכולין להפרד זה מזה וגם כתוב בסמוך:
rashi.eng: *and he assembled the house of Judah and Benjamin.* who were together on the border. Jerusalem belonged to both of them, and the Temple was built on their common border. In the section dealing with boundaries in Joshua, it explains how their border was shared. Our Rabbis also said (Yoma 12a, Meg. 26a, Zeb. 53b): A strip protruded from the territory of Benjamin and entered the territory of Judah, upon which the altar was built. Therefore, they were inseparable, and they are also mentioned close to one another.

notes.356: (tn, Heb): “and the word of the Lord came to Shemaiah the man of God, saying.”

notes.357: (tn, Heb): “for his thing is from me.”
notes.358: (tn, Heb): “and they heard the words of the Lord and returned from going against Jeroboam.”

rashi.heb:
*עם אחיכם.* 
והלא אחיכם בני איש אחד:
rashi.eng: *with your brothers.* Are they not your brothers, the sons of one man?

notes.359: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

rashi.heb:
*ויבן ערים למצור.* 
ערים קטנים בנה וסבב כל סביבותם מים משום חוזק וזה מצור כדאמרינן (בישעיהו ל״ז:כ״ה-כ״ו) אני קרתי ושתיתי מים ואחריב בכף פעמי כל יאורי מצור ועתה הוצרך לכך כי פשעו בו ישראל:
rashi.eng: *and he built cities for fortification.* Heb. לְמָצוֹר. He built small cities and surrounded them with water for strength, and this is [called] מָצוֹר as it is written in Isaiah (37:25): “I dug and drank water, and I dried up with the soles of my feet all rivers of fortification (מָצוֹר).” And this was now necessary because Israel rebelled against him.

notes.360: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map7-E2; Map8-E2; Map10-B4.

rashi.heb:
*ויתן בהם נגידים.* 
שרים ונציבים לשמור הערים והכרכים:
rashi.eng: *leaders.* chiefs and officers to guard the towns and the large cities.

rashi.heb:
*ואוצרות מאכל ושמן ויין.* 
לפי שיהא להם מאכל מזומן אם יעלו בית ישראל למצור:
rashi.eng: *and storehouses of food, oil, and wine.* in order to have food prepared for them should the house of Israel march upon them to besiege them.

notes.361: (tn, Heb): “he strengthened them greatly, very much.”

notes.362: (tn, Heb): “and the priests and the Levites who were in all Israel supported him from all their territory.”

rashi.heb:
*כי עזבו הלוים את מגרשיהם.* 
שבכל ארץ עשרת השבטים:
rashi.eng: *For the Levites had abandoned their open land.* that was in the entire land of the ten tribes.

rashi.heb:
*כי הזניחם ירבעם.* 
הזניחם מלעבוד ומכהן לה':
rashi.eng: *because Jeroboam… had coerced them to abandon.* He coerced them to abandon serving and ministering to the Lord.

notes.363: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Jeroboam) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.365: (tn, Heb): “and for the goats and for the calves he had made.”

rashi.heb:
*כהנים לבמות.* 
כלומר למה הזניח ירבעם הכהנים והלוים לפי שהעמיד כהנים כומרים לשעירים:
rashi.eng: *priests for the high places.* i.e., Why did Jeroboam coerce them to abandon [their positions]? Because he stationed pagan priests for the satyrs.

notes.366: (tn, Heb): “and after them from all the tribes of Israel, the ones giving their heart[s] to seek the Lord God of Israel came [to] Jerusalem.”

rashi.heb:
*ואחריהם.* 
של לוים וכהנים:
rashi.eng: *And after them.* [i.e., after] the Levites and the priests.

notes.370: (tn, Heb): “they walked in the way of.”

notes.372: (tn): The words “and of” are supplied in the translation for clarification and for stylistic reasons.

rashi.heb:
*אביהיל בת אליאב.* 
כמו ואביהיל לפני שמואל ואמר (שמואל א י״ז:ל״א) אך נגד ה' משיחו זה שהקב"ה עתיד לומר קום נא משחהו כי הוא זה וטעה בו שמואל שראה בתו של אליאב אשת רחבעם מלכה ועל זה הדבר נענש כשמואל כי ששאל לו שאול איזה בית הרואה (שם א' ט') ויאמר שמואל אנכי הרואה שלא ענהו דרך ענוה לומר מה תרצה אמר לו הקב"ה חייך אתה עתיד לראות ולא תדע מה תראה כי טעה באליאב ובתו המלכה:
rashi.eng: *Abihail the daughter of Eliab.* Like: and Abihail, similar to (Jer. 11:19): “And I was like a lamb and a bull כְּכֶבֶשׂ אַלּוּף.” The following was the reason that Samuel the seer erred when Jesse passed Eliab before Samuel, and he [Samuel] said, (I Sam. 16:6): “Surely before the Lord is His anointed.” This is the one about whom the Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to say, “Arise, anoint him, for this is he.” But Samuel erred about him, for he saw Eliab’s daughter as Rehoboam’s wife, the queen, and because of the following matter, Samuel was punished: When Saul asked him, (ibid. 9:18) “Which is the house of the seer?” Samuel replied, “I am the seer,” in which case he did not answer him with humility, saying, “What do you wish.” [Therefore,] the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him, “By your life, you are destined to see, and you will not know what you see,” for he erred concerning Eliab and his daughter the queen.

notes.373: (sn): Concubines were slave women in ancient Near Eastern societies who were the legal property of their master, but who could have legitimate sexual relations with their master. A concubine’s status was more elevated than a mere servant, but she was not free and did not have the legal rights of a free wife. The children of a concubine could, in some instances, become equal heirs with the children of the free wife. After the period of the Judges concubines may have become more of a royal prerogative (2 Sam 21:10-14; 1 Kgs 11:3).

notes.374: (tn, Heb): “and Rehoboam appointed for a head Abijah son of Maacah for ruler among his brothers, indeed to make him king.”

rashi.heb:
*לנגיד באחיו.* 
כדי להמליכו:
rashi.eng: *as a leader among his brothers.* in order to make him king.

notes.375: (tn, Heb): “and he was discerning and broke up from all his sons to all the lands of Judah and Benjamin, to all the fortified cities.”
notes.376: (tn): “and he asked for a multitude of wives.”

rashi.heb:
*ויפרץ.* 
פזר בניו לכל ארצות יהודה דוגמא (לעיל א' ד') ובית אביהם פרצו לרוב:
rashi.eng: *and he dispersed.* He scattered his sons to all the lands of Judah. A similar expression is (I Chron. 4:38): “And their fathers’ houses spread (פָּרְצוּ) exceedingly.”

notes.377: (tn, Heb): “also I have rejected you into the hand of Shishak.”

notes.378: (tn): Or “fair,” meaning the Lord’s punishment of them was just or fair.

notes.379: (tn, Heb): “the word of the Lord came to Shemaiah, saying.”
notes.380: (tn, Heb): “and I will give to them soon deliverance.”

rashi.heb:
*נכנעו לא אשחיתם.* 
דוגמא למטה (יד) עודנו הארץ לפנינו כי דרשנו ה' אלהינו דרשנו וגו', כן דרך הפסוק כשמפסיק בנתים כופל עוד התיב' לאומרה דוגמא (מדבר י') והיה כי תלך עמנו והיה הטוב וגו':
rashi.eng: *They have humbled themselves; I shall not destroy them.* A similar instance is found below (14:6): “The land is still before us for we have sought, etc. we have sought.” So is the custom of the Scriptures, that when it interrupts in the middle, it repeats the word. An example is (Num. 10:32): "And it will be, if you go with us, it will be that the good, etc.

notes.383: (tn, Heb): “so they may know my service and the service of the kingdoms of the lands.”

rashi.heb:
*כי יהיו לו לעבדים.* 
לשישק ולשאר עובדי כוכבים כמפורש:
rashi.eng: *For they will be his slaves.* [i.e., slaves] of Shishak and the other nations, as is explained.

rashi.heb:
*וידעו עבודתי.* 
כשישובו לא יהיה עליהם שום מושל ממלכי עובדי כוכבי' אבל כשתשובו מאחרי תורתי תדעו עבודת מלכי הארצות ותעבדו לה':
rashi.eng: *and they will know My service.* When they repent, no ruler of the kings of the nations will be over them, but when you abandon My Law, you will experience servitude to the kings of the lands, and you will serve them.

rashi.heb:
*והפקיד על יד שרי הרצים.* 
לקח המגינים מבית יער הלבנון והפקידם לשרי הרצים ואח"כ השיבם :
rashi.eng: *and he entrusted them in the hands of the chiefs of the runners.* He took them from the house of the forest of Lebanon and entrusted them to the chiefs of the runners and afterwards they returned them.

notes.385: (tn, Heb): “to the chamber of the runners.”

rashi.heb:
*אל תא הרצים.* 
חדר הרצים, כלומר אל מקומם, ענין אחר מפי מורי לפי שהיה דואג ממלך מצרים וממלך ישראל היו נושאין אותן לפניו:
rashi.eng: *to the chamber of the runners.* The room of the runners, i.e., to their place. Another explanation I heard from my mentor is that because he was afraid of the king of Egypt and the king of Israel, they would carry them [the shields] before him.

notes.386: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Rehoboam) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.387: (tn, Heb): “the anger of the Lord turned from him and did not destroy completely.”
notes.388: (tn, Heb): “and also in Judah there were good things.”

rashi.heb:
*ובהכנעו שב ממנו חרון אף ה'.* 
היה לו לומר למעלה מיד כשאמר ויעל שישק וגומר אלא שהפסיק בנתים לצורך ויעש תחתיהם מגיני נחשת:
rashi.eng: *And when he humbled himself, the Lord’s wrath returned from him.* He should have stated this above immediately when he said, “And Shishak… marched,” but he interrupted in between because he had to mention, “And… made instead of them shields of copper.”

notes.389: (tn, Heb): “and the king, Rehoboam, strengthened himself in Jerusalem and ruled.”
notes.390: (tn, Heb): “Rehoboam.” The recurrence of the proper name here is redundant in terms of contemporary English style, so the pronoun has been used in the translation instead.
notes.391: (tn, Heb): “the city where the Lord chose to place his name from all the tribes of Israel.”
notes.392: (tn, Heb): “his”; the referent has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*ויתחזק המלך רחבעם.* 
ומפרש למה שהרי כשהומלך תחילה היה בן מ"א לפיכך היה בו כח וחוזק להתחזק מעצמו כי היה בן שנה כשמת דוד שהרי שלמה מלך מ' שנה ושלמה עדיין לא מלך כשנולד רחבעם נמצא שרחבעם היה בן מ"א כשמלך:
rashi.eng: *And King Rehoboam strengthened himself in Jerusalem.* And he explains why, because when he was first made king, he was forty-one years old; therefore, he had the strength and the power to strengthen himself. He was a year old when David died, for Solomon reigned forty years, and Solomon had not yet reigned when Rehoboam was born. We find that Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he reigned.

rashi.heb:
*העיר אשר בחר ה' לשום את שמו שם מכל שבטי ישראל.* 
אלא שנתקלקלו במעשיהם כדכתיב ויעש הרע כי לא הכין לבו לדרוש את ה' וגרמו שנסתלקה שכינה מהם וכאלו קובל ומפיגין על כך:
rashi.eng: *the city that the Lord had chosen wherein to place His name, out of all the tribes of Israel.* but they deteriorated in their deeds, as it is written: “And he did that which was evil, for he did not set his heart to seek the Lord,” and they caused the Shechinah to leave them, and it was as if they were complaining and demonstrating about that.

notes.393: (tn, Heb): “because he did not set his heart to seek the Lord.”

notes.394: (tn, Heb): “As for the events of Rehoboam, the former and the latter, are they not written?”

rashi.heb:
*בדברי שמעיה הנביא.* 
כל נביא ונביא היה כותב ספרו מה שהיה מתנבא וזהו שמעיה שאמר לעיל (ב' י"א) ולקמן (י"ב) מוכיח ויתר דברי אביה ודרכיו ודבריו כתובין במדרש הנביא עדו ספרו היה נקרא מדרש:
rashi.eng: *in the words of Shemaiah the prophet.* Every prophet would write his book, containing that which he prophesied, and this is the Shemaiah who was mentioned above (11:2, 12:5). And the verse written further (13:22), “And the rest of the deeds of Abijah and his ways and his words are written in the midrash of the prophet Iddo,” proves this, [that each prophet wrote a book of his prophecies, and] his [Iddo’s] book was called midrash.

notes.396: (sn): The phrase the City of David refers here to the fortress of Zion in Jerusalem, not to Bethlehem. See 2 Sam 5:7.

notes.397: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
notes.398: (tn): The parallel text in 1 Kgs 15:1 identifies his mother as “Maacah, the daughter of Abishalom” [=Absalom, 2 Chr 11:20). Although most English versions identify the mother’s father as Uriel of Gibeah, a number of English versions substitute the name “Maacah” here for the mother (e.g., NIV, NCV, CEV, NLT).

rashi.heb:
*שלש שנים מלך בירושלים.* 
ולא יותר כדמוכח במלכים ובשנת עשרים לירבעם מלך ישראל מלך אסא מלך יהודה נמצא שאפילו שלשה שנים שלמים לא מלך:
